problem.summary: 单图像超分辨率（SR）任务中，现有深度残差网络（如SRResNet）存在不必要的模块（如批归一化层），限制了性能；且大多数方法将不同放大倍数的超分辨率视为独立问题，需要为每个倍数训练单独的网络，效率低下。

motivation.summary: 通过优化残差网络架构（移除批归一化层）并扩大模型规模（增加特征通道数），可以显著提升单图像超分辨率性能。同时，利用不同放大倍数之间的相关性，设计一个统一的多尺度模型，以减少模型参数和训练时间。

core_idea.summary: 提出增强型深度超分辨率网络（EDSR）和多尺度深度超分辨率网络（MDSR）。EDSR通过移除批归一化层和采用残差缩放来优化残差块，并扩大模型深度和宽度以提升性能。MDSR通过共享主干网络和尺度特定模块，在一个模型中处理多个放大倍数。

method.summary: 1. 残差块优化：移除批归一化层，采用残差缩放（因子0.1）以稳定训练。2. 单尺度模型（EDSR）：基线模型有16个残差块和64个特征通道；最终模型（EDSR）有32个残差块和256个特征通道。3. 多尺度模型（MDSR）：共享主干网络（80个残差块），包含尺度特定的预处理模块（5×5卷积核）和上采样模块。4. 训练策略：使用L1损失函数，Adam优化器，学习率衰减；对于×3和×4模型，使用预训练的×2模型进行初始化。5. 测试时采用几何自集成策略（翻转和旋转输入图像）。

experiments.summary: 在DIV2K、Set5、Set14、B100、Urban100等基准数据集上评估。与Bicubic、A+、SRCNN、VDSR、SRResNet等方法比较。使用PSNR和SSIM作为评价指标。EDSR和MDSR在所有数据集和放大倍数上均优于现有方法。EDSR+和MDSR+（使用自集成）进一步提升了性能。模型在NTIRE2017超分辨率挑战赛中获得第一名。

claims.claim: 移除批归一化层可以提升超分辨率性能并减少GPU内存使用。
残差缩放可以稳定大模型的训练。
使用L1损失比L2损失能获得更好的收敛性。
预训练×2模型可以加速×3和×4模型的训练并提升性能。
多尺度模型（MDSR）在参数更少的情况下，性能与单尺度模型（EDSR）相当。
几何自集成策略可以在不增加模型参数的情况下提升性能。

limitations.limitation: 论文未详细讨论模型在不同退化类型（如未知退化）下的泛化能力。
多尺度模型（MDSR）的性能略低于单尺度模型（EDSR），尽管参数更少。
自集成策略在测试时增加了计算量（8倍推理）。
模型较大（EDSR有43M参数），可能不适合资源受限的设备。

nodes.title: 残差块优化
nodes.label: Residual Block Optimization
nodes.summary: 通过移除批归一化层和采用残差缩放来优化残差块，以提升性能和训练稳定性。
nodes.description: 在残差块中移除批归一化层，因为批归一化会归一化特征，限制了网络的范围灵活性。同时，采用残差缩放（因子0.1）来稳定训练，特别是在使用大量特征通道时。在测试阶段，缩放层可以集成到前一个卷积层中以提高计算效率。

nodes.title: 单尺度模型（EDSR）
nodes.label: Single-scale Model (EDSR)
nodes.summary: 增强型深度超分辨率网络，通过扩大模型规模（深度和宽度）来提升单尺度超分辨率性能。
nodes.description: 基线模型有16个残差块和64个特征通道。最终模型（EDSR）有32个残差块（B=32）和256个特征通道（F=256），并采用残差缩放（因子0.1）。模型不使用批归一化层，也不在残差块外使用ReLU激活函数。对于×3和×4模型，使用预训练的×2模型进行初始化。

nodes.title: 多尺度模型（MDSR）
nodes.label: Multi-scale Model (MDSR)
nodes.summary: 多尺度深度超分辨率网络，通过共享主干网络和尺度特定模块，在一个模型中处理多个放大倍数。
nodes.description: 共享主干网络有80个残差块（B=80）和64个特征通道（F=64）。包含尺度特定的预处理模块（两个5×5卷积核的残差块）和上采样模块。在训练时，每个小批量随机选择一个放大倍数，并只更新对应的模块。模型参数更少（约8M），但性能与单尺度模型相当。

nodes.title: 训练策略
nodes.label: Training Strategy
nodes.summary: 使用L1损失函数、Adam优化器、学习率衰减和预训练初始化来训练模型。
nodes.description: 使用L1损失函数（而不是L2），因为实验表明L1损失能提供更好的收敛性。使用Adam优化器（β1=0.9, β2=0.999, ε=10^-8），小批量大小为16。学习率初始化为10^-4，每2×10^5次更新减半。对于×3和×4模型，使用预训练的×2模型进行初始化，以加速训练并提升性能。

nodes.title: 几何自集成
nodes.label: Geometric Self-ensemble
nodes.summary: 在测试时通过翻转和旋转输入图像生成多个增强输入，然后平均输出，以提升性能而不增加模型参数。
nodes.description: 在测试时，对输入图像应用8种几何变换（包括恒等变换），生成8个增强输入。使用网络对每个增强输入进行超分辨率，然后对输出应用逆变换，最后平均所有输出。这相当于模型集成，但不需要额外训练。

nodes.title: 实验评估
nodes.label: Experimental Evaluation
nodes.summary: 在多个基准数据集上评估模型，与现有方法比较，并在NTIRE2017挑战赛中获胜。
nodes.description: 在DIV2K、Set5、Set14、B100、Urban100等数据集上评估。使用PSNR和SSIM作为指标。EDSR和MDSR在所有数据集和放大倍数上均优于现有方法（如Bicubic、A+、SRCNN、VDSR、SRResNet）。EDSR+和MDSR+（使用自集成）进一步提升了性能。模型在NTIRE2017超分辨率挑战赛中获得第一名。

edges.label: 优化残差块用于EDSR
edges.description: 残差块优化（移除批归一化、残差缩放）被应用于构建单尺度模型EDSR。

edges.label: 优化残差块用于MDSR
edges.description: 残差块优化也被应用于多尺度模型MDSR的主干网络。

edges.label: MDSR训练
edges.description: 多尺度模型MDSR使用所述训练策略进行训练，包括随机选择尺度。

edges.label: EDSR自集成
edges.description: 在测试时，EDSR模型使用几何自集成策略来提升性能。

edges.label: MDSR自集成
edges.description: 在测试时，MDSR模型也使用几何自集成策略。

edges.description: 单尺度模型EDSR在实验评估中与现有方法比较。

terms.definition: 增强型深度超分辨率网络，一种单尺度超分辨率模型，通过优化残差块和扩大模型规模来提升性能。
多尺度深度超分辨率网络，一种多尺度超分辨率模型，通过共享主干网络和尺度特定模块在一个模型中处理多个放大倍数。
在残差块的最后卷积层后放置常数缩放层（因子0.1），以稳定训练，特别是在使用大量特征通道时。
在测试时通过翻转和旋转输入图像生成多个增强输入，然后平均输出，以提升性能而不增加模型参数。
一种网络层，通过归一化特征来加速训练，但在超分辨率任务中可能限制网络的范围灵活性。
一个高质量（2K分辨率）图像数据集，用于图像恢复任务，包含800张训练图像、100张验证图像和100张测试图像。

steps.description: 1. 准备DIV2K数据集和其他基准数据集。
2. 实现残差块优化（移除批归一化层，添加残差缩放层）。
3. 构建单尺度模型（EDSR）和多尺度模型（MDSR）架构。
4. 使用L1损失函数和Adam优化器训练模型，学习率衰减。
5. 对于×3和×4模型，使用预训练的×2模型进行初始化。
6. 在测试时实现几何自集成策略。
7. 在基准数据集上评估模型，计算PSNR和SSIM。

metadata.title: Enhanced Deep Residual Networks for Single Image Super-Resolution
metadata.venue: 2017 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / CNN / Top-cited ML method paper
metadata.abstract: Recent research on super-resolution has progressed with the development of deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN). In particular, residual learning techniques exhibit improved performance. In this paper, we develop an enhanced deep super-resolution network (EDSR) with performance exceeding those of current state-of-the-art SR methods. The significant performance improvement of our model is due to optimization by removing unnecessary modules in conventional residual networks. The performance is further improved by expanding the model size while we stabilize the training procedure. We also propose a new multi-scale deep super-resolution system (MDSR) and training method, which can reconstruct high-resolution images of different upscaling factors in a single model. The proposed methods show superior performance over the state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets and prove its excellence by winning the NTIRE2017 Super-Resolution Challenge[26].

Abstract

Recent research on super-resolution has progressed with the development of deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN). In particular, residual learning techniques exhibit improved performance. In this paper, we develop an en- hanced deep super-resolution network (EDSR) with perfor- mance exceeding those of current state-of-the-art SR meth- ods. The signiﬁcant performance improvement of our model is due to optimization by removing unnecessary modules in conventional residual networks. The performance is further improved by expanding the model size while we stabilize the training procedure. We also propose a new multi-scale deep super-resolution system (MDSR) and training method, which can reconstruct high-resolution images of different upscaling factors in a single model. The proposed methods show superior performance over the state-of-the-art meth- ods on benchmark datasets and prove its excellence by win- ning the NTIRE2017 Super-Resolution Challenge [26]. 1. For the single-scale models (EDSR), we train the net- works as described in Sec. 3.2. The ×2 model is trained from scratch. After the model converges, we use it as a pre- trained network for other scales. At each update of training a multi-scale model (MDSR),

among ×2, ×3 and ×4. Only the modules that correspond to the selected scale are enabled and updated. Hence, scale- speciﬁc residual blocks and upsampling modules that corre- spond to different scales other than the selected one are not enabled nor updated. We train our networks using L1 loss instead of L2. Min-
imizing L2 is generally preferred since it maximizes the

PSNR. However, based on a series of experiments we em- pirically found that L1 loss provides better convergence than L2. The evaluation of this comparison is provided in Sec. 4.4 We implemented the proposed networks with the Torch7 framework and trained them using NVIDIA Titan X GPUs. It is beneﬁcial especially when the model size or training time matters. Although self-ensemble strategy keeps the total number of parameters same, we notice that it gives approximately same performance gain compared to conventional model ensemble method that requires in- dividually trained models. We denote the methods using self-ensemble by adding ’+’ postﬁx to the method name; i.e. EDSR+/MDSR+. Note that geometric self-ensemble is valid only for symmetric downsampling methods such as bicubic downsampling. 4.4. Evaluation on DIV2K Dataset We test our proposed networks on the DIV2K dataset. The proposed models successfully reconstruct the detailed textures and edges in the HR images and exhibit better-looking SR out- puts compared with the previous works. 5. NTIRE2017 SR Challenge This work is initially proposed for the purpose of par- ticipating in the NTIRE2017 Super-Resolution Challenge [26]. The challenge aims to develop a single image super- resolution system with the highest PSNR. In the challenge, there exist two tracks for different de- graders (bicubic, unknown) with three downsample scales (×2, 3, 4) each. Input images for the unknown track are not only downscaled but also suffer from severe blurring. Therefore, more robust mechanisms are required to deal with the second track. We submitted our two SR models (EDSR and MDSR) for each competition and prove that our algorithms are very robust to different downsampling con- ditions. Some results of our algorithms on the unknown downsampling track are illustrated in Fi...
ual scaling techniques to stably train large models. Our

proposed singe-scale model surpasses current models and achieves the state-of-the-art performance. Furthermore, we develop a multi-scale super-resolution network to reduce the model size and training time. With scale-dependent modules and shared main network, our multi-scale model can effectively deal with various scales of super-resolution in a uniﬁed framework. While the multi-scale model remains compact compared with a set of single-scale models, it shows comparable performance to the single-scale SR model. Our proposed single-scale and multi-scale models have achieved the top ranks in both the standard benchmark datasets and the DIV2K dataset.
